question: Compute Pearson correlations between all gene-methylation site pairs (all-vs-all) using DNA methylation beta values and gene expression values from the same samples. Apply Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction globally across all pairs. Identify gene-methylation site pairs with significant negative correlations (FDR < 0.05).

files.eval_guideline: Gene-site pairs must match the reference as an unordered set; correlation values within +/-1e-4, P-values and FDR values within 1% relative absolute error; column order, row order, and header labels may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files are named significant_results.tsv and are TSVs, which is the expected output for listing the significant negative gene-methylation correlations.

parameters.question: Compare tables of significant negative gene-methylation site Pearson correlations (BH FDR < 0.05). Gene-site pairs must match as an unordered set; correlation values within +/-1e-4; P-values and FDR values within 1% relative error; column order, row order, and header labels may differ.

files.strategy_reasoning: This is a deterministic Pearson correlation with BH FDR correction. The guideline asks for record-level matching of gene-site pairs as an unordered set, with numeric tolerances and freedom in column order, row order and header labels, which is what approximate handles.

align_plan.reasoning: Both tables have the same five column names, so each column maps to the column with the same name. The table is not transposed. Each row is one gene-methylation site pair, so the key is Gene plus Site together. The guideline says to compare the pairs as an unordered set. The reference is sorted by Gene/Site and the candidate is sorted by correlation, so row order is ignored and both tables are sorted by Gene,Site before comparing. The numeric columns (Correlation, P-value, FDR) are compared within the allowed tolerances and are not used as keys.

column_configs.name: Correlation
column_configs.reasoning: The guideline allows ±1e-4 absolute error. With |r| between about 0.8 and 0.9, that is roughly 1.2e-4 relative error. The sign matters because the task looks for negative correlations.

column_configs.name: P-value
column_configs.reasoning: The guideline sets 1% relative error for P-values. These values are very small, so relative error is the right measure.

column_configs.name: FDR
column_configs.reasoning: The guideline sets 1% relative error for Benjamini-Hochberg FDR values.

comparison_plan.overall_reasoning: Gene and Site are the ID columns. They are used only for alignment, so a matching pair set is checked when the rows are joined. The three numeric columns follow the evaluation guideline, and each uses cell-by-cell relative absolute error (RAE) with a cut-off. Correlation values have magnitudes of about 0.8 to 0.9. An absolute tolerance of ±1e-4 therefore works out to roughly 1.1e-4 to 1.25e-4 relative error, so 1.2e-4 is used. P-value and FDR use 1% RAE (0.01), as the guideline states. The sign of the correlation matters because the task asks for negative correlations, so absolute values are not compared.
